title: Figma
paragraphs: I completed an intensive 2-week Figma bootcamp focused on mastering fundamental interface design tools. Through this training, I learned to create simple layouts using frames, shape tools (ellipse, rectangle), and establish visual hierarchy through the layers panel. I can work with various assets like image imports (e.g., smartphones, globes) and organize components into groups for workflow efficiency. Concrete examples include designing a simple mobile application prototype with basic elements like buttons, search bars, and menu categories.

My practical experience includes creating basic illustrations with shape tools and text handling (typography) for design content. I've practiced color grading techniques and exporting designs to various formats. In team projects, I contributed to application page designs with components like 'Top Up & Bills', 'Featured Categories', and simple navigation elements. I also understand structured layer naming conventions (e.g., Group 3, Group 5) to facilitate collaboration.

Through specialized modules, I learned to create Instagram feed designs using basic auto layout features and style consistency. I'm familiar with the Figma workflow from artboard frame creation, asset placement, to final design export. For simple collaborative projects, I can work effectively in shared files with teams using basic commenting features, though I'm still developing more advanced prototyping and design system skills.

Currently, my Figma skills include creating static wireframes and high-fidelity designs for simple mobile applications with basic components. I continue practicing to enhance my understanding of more advanced auto layouts, component variants, and basic prototyping for simple interactions. The bootcamp has given me a strong foundation to develop more structured UI/design system skills in the future.

title: Github
paragraphs: I have foundational experience using GitHub for personal source code management. I can create new repositories, upload files through GitHub's web interface, and perform basic editing on project files. I understand how to make repositories public or private, as well as configure basic access permissions for sharing repositories collaboratively. Additionally, I've successfully deployed simple static websites using GitHub Pages by enabling this feature through repository settings.

My skills include using the most basic Git commands like commit and push through GitHub Desktop, though I'm not yet proficient with command line usage. I can view file change history and revert to previous versions when needed. For collaboration, I'm currently limited to granting repository access to others. I'm continuously learning to improve my understanding of more structured Git workflows.

title: HTML
paragraphs: I have learned and mastered various fundamental HTML concepts through the W3Schools platform, starting from an introduction to HTML document structure, using editors, to applying basic elements such as headings, paragraphs, and lists. My understanding includes how to build website frameworks with basic tags like <html>, <head>, and <body>, as well as utilizing attributes to adjust element behavior. Additionally, I'm familiar with text formatting techniques like bold, italic, or underline using <b>, <i>, and <u> tags, along with quotations and comments to improve code readability.

Beyond basic elements, I've mastered advanced features like creating links with <a> tags, embedding images via <img>, and setting favicons for website visual identity. I also understand the importance of layout management using block elements (like <div>) and inline elements, as well as applying classes and ids for CSS styling. My skills include creating structured data tables (<table>) and organized lists (<ul>, <ol>). Notably, I've studied JavaScript integration with HTML and the use of iframes (<iframe>) for embedding external content.

My experience also covers basic CSS optimization for visual presentation, such as setting colors, fonts, and layouts through style attributes or external files. I understand how to manage file paths to organize resources (images, CSS, JS) and head techniques for metadata like page titles (<title>) or character encoding. With this comprehensive understanding, I'm ready to develop interactive, well-structured, and responsive portfolio websites while continuing to explore advanced topics like semantic HTML5 or supporting frameworks.

title: Java
paragraphs: I have developed a strong understanding of object-oriented programming (OOP) in Java, covering fundamental concepts such as classes, objects, attributes, methods, constructors (both default and parameterized), and the four OOP pillars: encapsulation (implemented with getters-setters), inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction. Through my project files, I've practiced various design patterns including association, aggregation, and composition between classes. I also understand the implementation of access modifiers (public, private, protected) to control class member visibility and have created concrete examples in small projects like contact management systems, calculators, and to-do list applications.

My experience includes developing graphical user interfaces (GUI) using Java Swing, working with components such as JFrame, JPanel, JButton, JLabel, and JTextField. I've experimented with various layout managers (FlowLayout, BorderLayout, GridLayout) to organize GUI components. Additionally, I understand event handling to create interactive applications. For data processing, I'm comfortable working with Java data structures like ArrayList, LinkedList, HashMap, HashSet, Stack, and Queue, and understand when to use each structure based on algorithmic needs.

I have experience in database programming using JDBC for CRUD operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete). From examples I've created, I understand how to establish database connections, use prepared statements to prevent SQL injection, and handle result sets. I've also learned basic encryption techniques like password hashing with SHA-256 and symmetric encryption/decryption using AES. For more structured application development, I've begun implementing multilayer architecture by separating business logic, data access layer, and presentation layer in projects like task managers and personal finance apps.

At the algorithm level, I've practiced various programming techniques including loops (for, while, do-while), conditionals (if-else, switch), recursion, and basic sorting. I understand exception handling with try-catch blocks to create more robust code. Through my exercises, I can solve basic logic problems like string manipulation (removing vowels, binary conversion), mathematical calculations, and pattern creation with nested loops. I continue to sharpen my problem-solving skills by creating various small utility programs.

Currently, I'm deepening my understanding of advanced Java concepts like lambda expressions, stream API, multithreading, and computer networking. I'm also interested in learning modern frameworks like Spring Boot for enterprise application development. With my strong foundation in Java core and experience building various small applications, I'm ready to further develop these skills to build more complex and scalable systems.

Overall, my Java experience covers a broad spectrum from programming fundamentals to intermediate application development concepts. I can analyze requirements, design OOP-based solutions, implement them in well-structured Java code, and perform basic testing. I'm enthusiastic about continuing to learn and apply these skills to more challenging projects.

title: MySql
paragraphs: I have developed strong MySQL skills, particularly in writing and optimizing SQL queries for various database operations. From the examples I've worked on, I have a solid understanding of basic operations like SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE, as well as aggregate functions including COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX. I've practiced using WHERE clauses for data filtering, GROUP BY for data grouping, and HAVING for filtering aggregate results. Additionally, I'm comfortable with data sorting using ORDER BY (both ascending and descending) and limiting query results with LIMIT. Concrete examples include queries to find employees with highest/lowest salaries, calculate average salaries per department, and display data with specific criteria.

My experience also includes complex table joins (JOIN), including INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, and subqueries to access data from multiple related tables. I've created queries connecting employees, departments, and job_history tables to extract information such as employee job histories or lists of departments with highest salaries. My understanding of table aliasing helps simplify queries involving multiple tables. I've also practiced using subqueries in both WHERE and FROM clauses, such as finding employees with salaries above their department average or displaying department data containing employees with specific criteria.

At the database design level, I have experience creating entity-relationship diagrams (ERD) covering entities like semesters, courses, professors, and their relationships. I understand database normalization concepts up to third normal form (3NF) and can apply them in database schema design. From the diagrams I've created, you can see my understanding of relationship cardinality (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) and use of primary keys/foreign keys to maintain referential integrity. I'm also familiar with creating views to simplify access to complex data and using indexes to improve query performance.

For more advanced database operations, I've studied transaction techniques to maintain data consistency, as well as basics of stored procedures and triggers. I also understand the importance of database security by implementing proper access rights and input sanitization to prevent SQL injection. My experience includes query optimization with EXPLAIN to analyze execution plans, as well as strategic indexing techniques to speed up queries on large tables. I continue to develop these skills by learning more advanced MySQL features like window functions, CTEs (Common Table Expressions), and table partitioning.

Overall, I have a strong foundation in SQL and MySQL database administration. My skills range from database design, writing complex queries, to performance optimization. I'm ready to apply these skills in database-driven application development requiring efficient and reliable data manipulation. Moving forward, I plan to deepen my knowledge of database clustering, replication, and backup/recovery techniques at enterprise scale.

title: PHP
paragraphs: I have developed fundamental PHP programming skills, particularly in building efficient code structures and interacting with HTML. Through various examples I've worked on, I understand how to use loops like for and foreach to display dynamic data, such as creating tables with automatically generated rows and columns. I've also practiced using if-else conditions to control display based on specific logic, like applying different colors to table rows depending on whether they're odd or even numbered. Additionally, I'm familiar with basic PHP syntax including variables, arrays, and string concatenation.

My experience also includes working with PHP arrays, both numeric and associative. I've created simple biodata lists by utilizing foreach loops to display each array element in HTML lists. I understand how to work with multidimensional arrays, such as storing person data with attributes (name, phone number, hobbies) and displaying them in an organized structure. While still developing these skills, I continue practicing to better understand how to manage more complex data using such array structures.

Furthermore, I've begun exploring database connections using PHP. I understand the basic concepts of connecting to MySQL databases through mysqli_connect and PDO (PHP Data Objects), including error handling with try-catch. I've also learned to set up backend development environments, such as creating database connection configuration files and understanding the importance of security when managing credentials. While my implementations are still simple, I have sufficient foundation to develop database-connected applications in the future.

I also have initial experience building backend logic for web applications, such as creating simple login/register systems and managing product or category data (as seen in my project directory structures). I'm continuing to learn how to build basic APIs with PHP to handle HTTP requests and interact with frontend. Moving forward, I plan to delve into PHP frameworks like Laravel or CodeIgniter, while strengthening my understanding of web security and database query optimization.

Overall, I have a solid foundation in basic PHP syntax and have practiced important concepts like loops, conditions, arrays, and database connections. I'm excited to continue honing these skills by building more complex projects and learning advanced topics like user authentication, RESTful APIs, and integration with modern frontend technologies.

title: Python
paragraphs: I have developed fundamental Python understanding through various exercises and small projects. From the files I've worked on, I grasp basic Python programming concepts like variables, data types, operators, and control structures (conditional statements with if-else and loops). I've practiced creating functions both with and without parameters, including functions with return values. Concrete examples include basic exercises like simple mathematical operations, string manipulation, and basic input/output processing.

My experience includes working with Python data structures such as lists, tuples, and dictionaries. I understand how to access, add, modify, and remove elements in these data structures. I've also learned basic object-oriented programming (OOP) concepts in Python including class creation, objects, constructors, inheritance, and method overriding. From my project files, you can see my understanding in creating simple modules and using them through import statements, both directly and with from-import.

I've practiced basic file handling operations like reading and writing text files (file.txt). For further development, I'm continuing to study intermediate concepts like exception handling, decorators, and generators. My current Python skills include creating small programs that can solve basic computational problems and simple data manipulation. I plan to deepen my understanding of more complex data structures and application development using Python frameworks.

title: R programming
paragraphs: I have developed fundamental R programming skills for data analysis, including manipulation of data structures like vectors, lists, matrices, and data frames. From the examples I've worked on, I understand how to create and access elements within these data structures, as well as perform basic operations like filtering (data_frame[data_frame$value >= 85]), adding new columns (data_frame$grade), and removing specific rows. I've also practiced using basic R functions like sum(), paste(), and ifelse() for simple data processing.

My experience includes using dplyr and tidyr packages for data manipulation, including operations like column renaming (rename()), selecting specific columns (select()), filtering data based on conditions (filter()), data sorting (arrange()), and creating new variables (mutate()). I understand how to use the pipe operator (%>%) to efficiently chain multiple data operations. Concrete examples include e-commerce dataset analysis calculating total AOV per region and average Purchase Frequency using group_by() and summarise().

For data visualization, I've practiced creating various plots using ggplot2, including scatter plots (geom_point()), line plots (geom_line()), bar charts (geom_bar()), and histograms (geom_histogram()). I understand how to add titles, labels, and themes (labs(), theme_minimal()) as well as faceting techniques (facet_wrap(), facet_grid()) for multidimensional visualization. I can also customize plots with multiple layers like adding trendlines (geom_smooth()).

Regarding data cleaning, I've practiced handling missing values with deletion methods (na.omit()) and mean imputation (is.na()), as well as transforming data from wide to long format using pivot_wider(). For statistical analysis, I understand basic linear regression concepts and model evaluation using R-squared and RMSE metrics, though still at an introductory level. I continue to develop skills in reading data from various sources (read_excel()) and basic data exploration (str(), summary()).

Overall, my R skills cover the complete data analysis workflow from data import, cleaning, manipulation, to basic visualization. I can apply these techniques to solve simple data analysis problems and present insights through informative visualizations. Moving forward, I plan to learn more advanced analysis techniques like time series analysis and basic machine learning using R.

title: WordPress
paragraphs: I have foundational experience in using WordPress to build and design web pages. Although still at a beginner level, I already understand how to manage content using the Gutenberg editor, such as adding text blocks, images, and buttons. I'm also familiar with basic display configuration by utilizing default WordPress themes and adjusting some settings like colors, fonts, and simple layouts.

Additionally, I've experimented with installing and activating basic plugins to enhance website functionality, such as contact form plugins and simple SEO tools. I've also learned how to upload media to the WordPress library and incorporate them into posts or pages. This experience has given me a fundamental understanding of the WordPress workflow and its potential as a user-friendly web development platform.

Looking ahead, I plan to further develop my WordPress skills by studying more complex themes, additional CSS customization, and exploring more advanced plugins. With the foundation I've already established, I'm confident I can continue to improve my WordPress capabilities.
